periodic table.definition: The periodic table organizes chemical elements based on their atomic number, electron configuration, and chemical properties.

groups.alkali metals: Group 1 elements, highly reactive, including lithium (Li), sodium (Na), potassium (K), rubidium (Rb), cesium (Cs), and francium (Fr).
groups.alkaline earth metals: Group 2 elements, reactive but less so than alkali metals, including beryllium (Be), magnesium (Mg), calcium (Ca), strontium (Sr), barium (Ba), and radium (Ra).
groups.transition metals: Groups 3-12, characterized by metallic properties and multiple oxidation states, including iron (Fe), copper (Cu), and gold (Au).
groups.halogens: Group 17, highly reactive nonmetals including fluorine (F), chlorine (Cl), bromine (Br), iodine (I), and astatine (At).
groups.noble gases: Group 18, inert gases that are chemically stable, including helium (He), neon (Ne), argon (Ar), krypton (Kr), xenon (Xe), and radon (Rn).
groups.lanthanides: Rare earth metals from atomic numbers 57-71, including lanthanum (La), cerium (Ce), and neodymium (Nd).
groups.actinides: Radioactive elements from atomic numbers 89-103, including uranium (U), plutonium (Pu), and thorium (Th).

periodic table.periods: The periodic table is arranged in 7 horizontal periods that represent energy levels of electrons.
periodic table.atomic number: The atomic number of an element represents the number of protons in its nucleus.
periodic table.atomic mass: Atomic mass is the average mass of an element's isotopes, measured in atomic mass units (amu).
periodic table.isotopes: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons but the same number of protons.
periodic table.electronegativity: Electronegativity is the ability of an atom to attract electrons in a chemical bond; fluorine (F) has the highest electronegativity.
periodic table.ionization energy: Ionization energy is the energy required to remove an electron from an atom.
periodic table.metallic and non-metallic properties: Metals are generally conductive, malleable, and ductile, while nonmetals are brittle and poor conductors.

basic physics.newton's laws: Newton's three laws describe motion and force, including inertia, acceleration, and action-reaction.
basic physics.energy: Energy is the capacity to do work and exists in many forms such as kinetic, potential, thermal, and chemical.
basic physics.speed and velocity: Speed is the rate of movement, while velocity is speed in a specific direction.
basic physics.force: A force is a push or pull that can cause an object to accelerate, decelerate, or change direction.
basic physics.momentum: Momentum is the product of an object's mass and velocity, representing the quantity of motion.

basic chemistry.atoms and molecules: Atoms are the basic units of matter, while molecules are combinations of two or more atoms.
basic chemistry.states of matter: Matter exists in solid, liquid, gas, and plasma states, depending on temperature and pressure.
basic chemistry.chemical reactions: A chemical reaction occurs when substances combine or break apart to form new substances.
basic chemistry.acids and bases: Acids release hydrogen ions in solution, while bases release hydroxide ions.
basic chemistry.oxidation and reduction: Oxidation involves losing electrons, while reduction involves gaining electrons.

basic biology.cells: Cells are the basic structural and functional units of life, classified as prokaryotic or eukaryotic.
basic biology.organ systems: The human body consists of organ systems such as circulatory, respiratory, digestive, nervous, and skeletal systems.
basic biology.genetics: Genetics is the study of heredity, genes, and DNA inheritance patterns.
basic biology.microorganisms: Microorganisms include bacteria, viruses, fungi, and protists, some of which cause diseases.
basic biology.enzymes: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions in the body.

basic astronomy.solar system: The Solar System consists of the Sun, eight planets, moons, asteroids, and comets.
basic astronomy.galaxies: Galaxies are vast systems of stars, gas, and dust bound by gravity. The Milky Way is our home galaxy.
basic astronomy.big bang theory: The Big Bang Theory explains the origin of the universe, stating it began as a singularity and expanded rapidly.
basic astronomy.light years: A light-year is the distance light travels in one year, approximately 9.46 trillion kilometers.
basic astronomy.nebulae: Nebulae are giant clouds of gas and dust in space, where new stars are born.

earth sciences.rock cycle: The rock cycle explains how rocks transform between igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic forms.
earth sciences.plate tectonics: Plate tectonics describes the movement of Earth's lithospheric plates, causing earthquakes, mountains, and volcanoes.
earth sciences.volcanoes: Volcanoes are openings in Earth's crust where magma, ash, and gases erupt.
earth sciences.earthquakes: Earthquakes occur when Earth's tectonic plates move, releasing energy in the form of seismic waves.
earth sciences.ocean currents: Ocean currents are large-scale water movements driven by wind, temperature, and salinity differences.

human body.respiratory system: The respiratory system allows breathing, bringing oxygen into the body and expelling carbon dioxide.
human body.circulatory system: The circulatory system consists of the heart, blood, and blood vessels, transporting oxygen and nutrients.
human body.digestive system: The digestive system breaks down food into nutrients that the body can absorb and use for energy.
human body.immune system: The immune system defends the body against pathogens using white blood cells and antibodies.
human body.nervous system: The nervous system controls bodily functions through neurons and the brain, including sensory perception and movement.

technology and innovation.electricity: Electricity is the flow of electric charge, powering devices and lighting up homes.
technology and innovation.magnetism: Magnetism is the force exerted by magnets, attracting or repelling certain metals.
technology and innovation.renewable energy: Renewable energy comes from sources like solar, wind, hydro, and geothermal power, reducing environmental impact.
technology and innovation.nuclear energy: Nuclear energy is produced from nuclear reactions, used for power generation and medicine.
technology and innovation.space exploration: Space exploration includes studying celestial bodies and launching satellites, space probes, and astronauts into space.

math.pi: Pi is approximately equal to 3.14159, representing the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter.
math.fibonacci: The Fibonacci sequence starts with 0 and 1, and each subsequent number is the sum of the previous two.
math.pythagoras theorem: In a right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of squares of the other two sides, expressed as a² + b² = c².
math.quadratic formula: The quadratic formula is used to solve equations in the form ax² + bx + c = 0, and is given by x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) / 2a.
math.calculus: Calculus is the mathematical study of continuous change, with two major branches: differential calculus and integral calculus.
math.trigonometry: Trigonometry is the branch of mathematics dealing with relationships between the sides and angles of triangles, particularly the sine, cosine, and tangent functions.
math.logarithm: A logarithm is the inverse operation to exponentiation, answering the question: to what power must a given number be raised to produce another number?
math.euler's identity: Euler's identity, e^(iπ) + 1 = 0, is considered one of the most beautiful equations in mathematics, linking five fundamental mathematical constants.
math.statistics: Statistics is the discipline that concerns the collection, organization, analysis, interpretation, and presentation of data.
math.probability: Probability is the branch of mathematics concerning numerical descriptions of how likely an event is to occur, or how likely a proposition is to be true.

basic calculations.addition: Addition is combining two or more numbers to get a total sum.
basic calculations.subtraction: Subtraction is finding the difference between two numbers.
basic calculations.multiplication: Multiplication is repeated addition of a number.
basic calculations.division: Division is splitting a number into equal parts.
basic calculations.modulus: Modulus is the remainder when one number is divided by another.
basic calculations.percentage: Percentage is a fraction expressed as a number out of 100.
basic calculations.average: Average is the sum of values divided by the number of values.

history.world war 2: World War II lasted from 1939 to 1945, involving most nations, including all great powers, forming opposing military alliances: the Allies and the Axis.
history.french revolution: The French Revolution was a period of radical social and political upheaval in France from 1789 to 1799.
history.ancient egypt: Ancient Egyptian civilization thrived along the Nile River from about 3100 BC to 332 BC, known for its pyramids, pharaohs, and hieroglyphics.
history.roman empire: The Roman Empire was the post-Republican period of ancient Rome, characterized by an autocratic form of government lasting from 27 BC to 476 AD in the West.
history.renaissance: The Renaissance was a period of European cultural, artistic, political, and scientific rebirth following the Middle Ages, spanning the 14th to 17th centuries.
history.industrial revolution: The Industrial Revolution was the transition to new manufacturing processes in Europe and the United States from about 1760 to 1840.
history.cold war: The Cold War was a period of geopolitical tension between the United States and the Soviet Union and their allies from 1945 to 1991.
history.american revolution: The American Revolution was a colonial revolt that occurred between 1765 and 1783, establishing the United States of America.
history.civil rights movement: The Civil Rights Movement was a struggle for social justice that took place mainly during the 1950s and 1960s for Black Americans to gain equal rights.
history.ancient greece: Ancient Greece was a civilization belonging to a period of Greek history that flourished from the 8th to 6th centuries BC to the end of antiquity.
history.world war 1: World War I was a global conflict that lasted from 1914 to 1918, originating in Europe and resulting in an estimated 9 million combatant deaths.
history.colonialism: Colonialism is the policy of a country seeking to extend or retain its authority over other peoples or territories, generally with the aim of economic dominance.
history.mesopotamia: Mesopotamia was a historical region situated within the Tigris–Euphrates river system, in modern days roughly corresponding to Iraq and parts of Syria, Turkey, and Iran.
history.byzantine empire: The Byzantine Empire was the continuation of the Roman Empire in its eastern provinces, lasting from 330 AD to 1453 AD.
history.mongol empire: The Mongol Empire, founded by Genghis Khan in 1206, became the largest contiguous land empire in history.
history.ottoman empire: The Ottoman Empire was a powerful Islamic empire that lasted from 1299 to 1922, controlling large parts of Europe, Asia, and Africa.
history.middle ages: The Middle Ages, or medieval period, lasted from the 5th to the 15th century, marked by feudalism, knights, and the spread of Christianity in Europe.
history.great depression: The Great Depression was a severe global economic crisis that started in 1929 and lasted through the 1930s, marked by widespread unemployment and poverty.
history.vietnam war: The Vietnam War (1955-1975) was a conflict in Vietnam, Laos, and Cambodia, with North Vietnam (communist) fighting against South Vietnam and its U.S. allies.
history.scientific revolution: The Scientific Revolution (16th-18th centuries) was a period of major scientific advancements that laid the foundation for modern science.
history.american civil war: The American Civil War (1861-1865) was a conflict between the Northern states (Union) and the Southern states (Confederacy) over slavery and state rights.
history.persian empire: The Persian Empire, founded by Cyrus the Great in 550 BC, was one of the largest and most influential empires in history.
history.trojan war: The Trojan War, described in Greek mythology and Homer's epic poems, was fought between the Greeks and the city of Troy around the 12th century BC.
history.crusades: The Crusades (1096-1291) were a series of religious wars between Christians and Muslims over control of the Holy Land.
history.fall of constantinople: The Fall of Constantinople in 1453 marked the end of the Byzantine Empire and the rise of the Ottoman Empire.
history.napoleonic wars: The Napoleonic Wars (1803-1815) were a series of wars led by Napoleon Bonaparte, reshaping Europe's political landscape.
history.black death: The Black Death (1347-1351) was a devastating global epidemic of the bubonic plague that killed millions in Europe and Asia.

geography.continents: There are seven continents: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia, Europe, North America, and South America.
geography.oceans: The five oceans are the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, and Arctic Ocean.
geography.mount everest: Mount Everest is Earth's highest mountain above sea level, located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas.
geography.amazon rainforest: The Amazon Rainforest is the world's largest tropical rainforest, covering much of northwestern Brazil and extending into Colombia, Peru, and other South American countries.
geography.sahara desert: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world, covering most of North Africa.
geography.great barrier reef: The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef system, located off the coast of Queensland, Australia.
geography.nile river: The Nile is the longest river in Africa and has historically been considered the longest river in the world.
geography.grand canyon: The Grand Canyon is a steep-sided canyon carved by the Colorado River in Arizona, United States.
geography.himalayas: The Himalayas are a mountain range in Asia separating the plains of the Indian subcontinent from the Tibetan Plateau.
geography.capital cities: Some notable capital cities include Washington D.C. (USA), London (UK), Beijing (China), Moscow (Russia), Tokyo (Japan), and Paris (France).
geography.countries: There are 195 countries in the world, including 193 member states of the United Nations plus the Holy See and the State of Palestine.
geography.plate tectonics: Plate tectonics is the theory that Earth's outer shell is divided into several plates that glide over the mantle, the rocky inner layer above the core.
geography.population: The world population was approximately 8 billion people as of 2023, with China and India being the most populous countries.

Andhra Pradesh.description: Located in southeastern India, known for its Telugu culture, temples, and rich agricultural lands.

Arunachal Pradesh.description: Northeastern state known for its stunning mountain ranges and diverse tribal culture.

Assam.description: Famous for Assam tea, the Kaziranga National Park, and the Brahmaputra River.

Bihar.description: A historic state in eastern India, known for Nalanda University and Buddhist pilgrimage sites.

Chhattisgarh.description: Known for its forests, waterfalls, and tribal culture.

Goa.description: A popular tourist destination known for its beaches, Portuguese heritage, and nightlife.

Gujarat.description: Known for Gir National Park (home to Asiatic lions), the Rann of Kutch, and its industrial development.

Haryana.description: A leading agricultural state, home to important historical sites and modern infrastructure.

Himachal Pradesh.description: A beautiful hill state famous for its scenic mountains, tourism, and apple orchards.

Jharkhand.description: Rich in minerals, forests, and waterfalls.

Karnataka.description: Known as India's IT hub, home to historic sites like Hampi and modern industries.

Kerala.description: Famous for its backwaters, ayurvedic treatments, and high literacy rate.

Madhya Pradesh.description: Central India's largest state, known for historical monuments and wildlife sanctuaries.

Maharashtra.description: Home to India's financial capital, Bollywood, and the historic Ajanta and Ellora caves.

Manipur.description: Known for its rich culture, Loktak Lake, and sports talents.

Meghalaya.description: A northeastern state known for its hills, waterfalls, and unique matrilineal society.

Mizoram.description: A scenic hilly state known for its tribal culture and handicrafts.

Nagaland.description: Known for its diverse tribal communities and the Hornbill Festival.

Odisha.description: Famous for Jagannath Temple, ancient rock-cut caves, and beautiful beaches.

Punjab.description: The land of five rivers, famous for Golden Temple and vibrant Sikh culture.

Rajasthan.description: The largest Indian state, famous for its deserts, palaces, and forts.

Sikkim.description: A small Himalayan state known for its biodiversity and beautiful monasteries.

Tamil Nadu.description: A cultural hub of South India, famous for its temples, beaches, and classical arts.

Telangana.description: Known for its IT industry, Charminar, and rich history.

Tripura.description: A small state in the northeast, rich in tribal culture and biodiversity.

Uttar Pradesh.description: India's most populous state, home to Taj Mahal and Varanasi.

Uttarakhand.description: Known for its scenic hill stations and pilgrimage sites.

West Bengal.description: Famous for its cultural heritage, Howrah Bridge, and Durga Puja.

Andaman and Nicobar Islands.description: A group of islands known for their pristine beaches and marine biodiversity.

Chandigarh.description: A well-planned city that serves as the capital of both Punjab and Haryana.

Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.description: A union territory known for its beaches and Portuguese heritage.

Lakshadweep.description: A group of coral atolls and islands, known for their scenic beauty.

Delhi.description: The capital of India, a historical and political center with landmarks like India Gate and Red Fort.

Puducherry.description: A former French colony known for its unique blend of French and Tamil culture.

Jammu and Kashmir.description: A beautiful region known for its mountains, valleys, and rich cultural history.

Ladakh.description: A high-altitude desert region known for its stunning landscapes and Buddhist monasteries.
